title: A woman grabbing his hand while he led the band
summary: While leading with his back to the floor, a blond white woman took hold of his hand and he kept his cool until the number ended.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That was really a -- that was really something. I'll tell you another thing. I had an experience -- you know, I was Louis' assistant, so Louis would play a number of dances, and Louis would go take a rest and I'd have to get up and take the band. Floor was just crowded. So I was up playing and directing the band, and after a while somebody just grabbed my hand. And I had my back turned to them, see, and they had my hand, holding it, you know. Floor was crowded. Then I noticed a look on the boys' -- the boys looked, I said, 'What's that (inaudible) got hold of my hand, and why are those guys looking so funny?' So when I turned around, this way, I turned around and there was this long-haired blond had hold of my hand. She had hold of my hand. And then -- I didn't object, I just come on and I kept my cool, you know. Of course, I was afraid if I'd jerk, it might jerk her down, see.
And I didn't want to do that, so I just kept my cool. And when they ended that number, she turned my hand loose and we just walked right on off the stand.
Of course, you had to be very careful down there with them people. They didn't -- at that time, they didn't understand.
